predictor.name: Mitchell Kapor (predictor) and Ray Kurzweil (challenger), on Long Bets

parties.name: Mitchell Kapor
parties.position: predictor: that by 2029 no computer will have passed the Turing Test

sourceDate.note: Bet duration "27 years (02002-02029)"; the page read is the live bet page.

records.event: By 2029 no computer - or "machine intelligence" - will have passed the Turing Test.
records.stakes: $20,000, to the Electronic Frontier Foundation if Kapor wins or the Kurzweil Foundation if Kurzweil wins (as stated on the page)
records.qualification: On the live page, the bet's statement is a negative prediction made by Kapor; Kurzweil is the challenger. The same page carries the "Detailed Terms" ("A Wager on the Turing Test: The Rules", "As prepared by Ray Kurzweil in consultation with Mitchell Kapor"), which set the judges and procedure. The live page does not authenticate the wording of 2002. An Internet Archive capture of 7 June 2002 (20020607200712), read by a reviewer from a different model family on 2026-11-05, states the bet differently: "A computer - or "machine intelligence" - will pass the Turing Test by 2029.", with "Mitchell Kapor (mkapor) initiator", "Ray Kurzweil (rkurzweil) responder" and "Stakes $20,000 ($10,000 each)". The record keeps the live wording, attested from 2026-11-02. No outcome is recorded.
